primary_source.title: Karimireddy et al., SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning
primary_source.method: Independently opened official PDF with web tool and read Algorithm 1 and equations 3-5; independently fetched exact PDF bytes with curl.

primary_source.interpretation: Main algorithm gives the subtractive local correction and ci-c displacement formula; population c uses 1/N, whereas model averaging uses 1/|S| with global rate. Appendix 19 reverses the two control terms. The algebraic telescope and counterexample identify that discrepancy independently; it is not adopted as the implementation oracle.

claim_assessment.subject: Correct Option II equations, sign and gradient-average identity

documentation.path: docs/docs/examples/algorithms/5. Algorithms with Customized Client Training Loops.md

claim_assessment.basis: after_step adds correction with alpha=-executed_rate; on_train_end uses old ci minus c plus displacement/(local_steps*rate), then subtracts old ci for delta. The main paper and independent telescope agree. The mean-gradient claim is explicitly bounded to constant-rate vanilla SGD.

claim_assessment.subject: V2 compatibility and Option I boundary

documentation.path: docs/docs/examples/algorithms/5. Algorithms with Customized Client Training Loops.md

claim_assessment.basis: V2 inherits corrected Option II without a separate accumulator or extra gradient pass. The prose retains the public name and does not promise true Option I or improved accuracy.

claim_assessment.subject: Actual optimizer rate constraints and timing

documentation.path: docs/docs/examples/algorithms/5. Algorithms with Customized Client Training Loops.md

claim_assessment.basis: The actual optimizer is published in context; a step pre-hook captures finite positive non-tensor scalar rates for groups owning trainable model parameters. Equal rates and constant rate within a local round are enforced before the affected step, with a new round reset. The correction uses the captured executed rate after later optimizer hooks.

claim_assessment.subject: Actual K, accumulation tail, skipped/zero updates and trainable ownership

documentation.path: docs/docs/examples/algorithms/5. Algorithms with Customized Client Training Loops.md

claim_assessment.basis: Only completed optimizer updates increment local_steps. A partial accumulation window normalizes its actual microbatch count and steps once; skipped steps do not correct/count. K=0 clones retained controls and generates fresh zeros. Parameter identity includes optimizer-owned trainables with no gradient; excluded trainables retain controls and have zero delta; frozen parameters and buffers receive no SCAFFOLD correction.

claim_assessment.subject: Population control update and separate sample-weighted model extension

documentation.path: docs/docs/examples/algorithms/5. Algorithms with Customized Client Training Loops.md

claim_assessment.basis: Server sums unweighted control deltas over the total client population. FedAvg separately weights models by positive total sample counts. The README conditions its explicit model formula on positive total count. Unequal counts and shipped momentum .9 are described as extensions with no imported paper convergence guarantee.

claim_assessment.subject: Momentum/Adam and other non-vanilla optimizer caveat; independent oracle attribution

documentation.path: docs/docs/examples/algorithms/5. Algorithms with Customized Client Training Loops.md

claim_assessment.basis: The post-optimizer additive correction does not enter momentum/Adam gradient history and warns for non-vanilla optimizers. Delivered tests use independent fixed scalar expectations, raw optimizer plus explicit correction, and retained rational multiround expectations. Those test assertions were inspected, not run here. No public prose exposes test counts or calls the shipped configuration paper-equivalent.

claim_assessment.subject: Current inbound payload and direct/spawn client result acceptance

documentation.path: docs/docs/examples/algorithms/5. Algorithms with Customized Client Training Loops.md

claim_assessment.basis: Inbound extraction clears stale controls/delta and installs the current validated server control. _train_model stages controls then runs training callbacks; train_model runs the fallible training-step end hook before direct acceptance. train_process defers acceptance through model save and exports provisional ci/delta/K/rate when spawned. Parent checks current token and client, loads model and validates control state before acceptance. Only acceptance atomically replaces canonical ci. Rejection restores pending prior controls and refuses outbound delta. No promise of independent child canonical writes or broader whole-experiment rollback is made. Fresh review3 F27-R3-01 shows the remaining direct-only cleanup gap: train_model accepts at line 454 and sets successful at 455 before fallible model-update cleanup at 463. An otherwise-successful cleanup exception can leave canonical controls advanced and outbound eligible. The documented after-all-end-hooks contract is required and must not be weakened. Client-control failure atomicity is conditional on the author correction and fresh final code/source reconciliation; it is not fully implemented on this pinned 15e candidate.

claim_assessment.subject: Server raw validation, post-receive-callback state, aggregation commit and failure bounds

documentation.path: docs/docs/examples/algorithms/5. Algorithms with Customized Client Training Loops.md

claim_assessment.basis: Raw model and control halves validate before staging. The callback wrapper forwards callbacks then revalidates the model/control state used, and checks resulting model/control values after aggregation callbacks. committed becomes true only after those callbacks and final checks. Precommit exception restores known model/control tensors; finally clears staging and restores handler. Evaluation/reporting happen afterward and retain a completed commit. External callback side effects are explicitly excluded. This writing assessment is source inspection, not independent closure of F27-R2-01.

claim_assessment.subject: Logical-client ownership, canonical state, exact historical structural imports

documentation.path: docs/docs/examples/algorithms/5. Algorithms with Customized Client Training Loops.md

claim_assessment.basis: The strategy owns ci and resolves scaffold_cv_ID.pkl under model_path or save_path. Canonical file wins; absent canonical permits exact same-client contained model_name_ID_control_variate.pth then historical root-prefix-concatenated pkl. Load failure does not fall through. Validation requires finite floating trainable tensors and correct shapes, ignores known frozen/buffer extras, and rejects unknown keys. Logical identity change clears old state; client 0 is not substituted. Saves leave distinct legacy files unchanged.

documentation.path: docs/docs/examples/algorithms/5. Algorithms with Customized Client Training Loops.md
